claim: Published at ICML 2015; arXiv 1503.03585 first posted March 2015
Slowly destroy structure in data with an iterative forward diffusion process, then learn a reverse diffusion process that restores it, giving a flexible yet tractable generative model
The method borrows the idea of a Markov chain that gradually converts one distribution into another from nonequilibrium statistical physics (Jarzynski equality) and annealed importance sampling
For small step size beta, the reverse of a Gaussian (binomial) diffusion step is also Gaussian (binomial), so only mean and covariance (or bit-flip rate) need be learned
value: reverse step has same functional form

claim: Training maximizes a lower bound K on log-likelihood made of per-step KL divergences between forward posteriors q(x^(t-1)|x^(t),x^(0)) and reverse steps, plus analytic entropy terms
